title: Lecture 1 — Practice Exam C: Mixed Review
subject: Programming Languages
description: Lecture 1 only. Original AI-generated practice questions based on the supplied handout; not an official exam or answer key.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT a benefit of studying programming language concepts listed in the lecture?
options: It removes the need to learn different languages
It increases the ability to express ideas
It improves use of already-known languages
It improves understanding of implementation
questions.correctAnswer: It removes the need to learn different languages
questions.explanation: The lecture says developers must be prepared to learn different languages; conceptual study supports learning rather than eliminating it.

questions.question: Which collection best matches the lecture's web-software domain?
options: Only scientific numerical languages
Markup, scripting, and general-purpose languages
Only machine languages
Only logic languages
questions.correctAnswer: Markup, scripting, and general-purpose languages
questions.explanation: The lecture describes web software as an eclectic collection including HTML, PHP, and Java examples.

questions.question: An operator means numeric addition in one context and combining objects in another. Which readability issue does this illustrate?
options: Fetch-execute sequencing
Executable loading
Operator overloading
Program portability
questions.correctAnswer: Operator overloading
questions.explanation: Operator overloading gives one symbol different meanings, which can increase what the reader must infer.

questions.question: A language requires exceptions to many rules for combining otherwise simple features. Which characteristic is weakened?
options: The number of available environments
Run-time error display
The size of source files
Orthogonality
questions.correctAnswer: Orthogonality
questions.explanation: Orthogonality depends on consistent combinations; numerous exceptions reduce predictability.

questions.question: Which pair contains characteristics that contribute to writability in the lecture?
options: Abstraction and expressivity
Aliasing and memory bandwidth
Linking and loading
Program counters and input devices
questions.correctAnswer: Abstraction and expressivity
questions.explanation: The lecture names simplicity/orthogonality, abstraction, and expressivity as writability characteristics.

questions.question: Why does the lecture prefer type checking at compile time when possible?
options: Compile-time checks make syntax analysis unnecessary
Run-time type checks add execution cost
Compile-time checks eliminate all logical errors
Run-time checks are impossible in every language
questions.correctAnswer: Run-time type checks add execution cost
questions.explanation: Checking before execution can avoid the cost of repeatedly checking during execution; it does not prove full correctness.

questions.question: A language forces programmers to express an algorithm in unnatural ways. What consequence does the lecture identify?
options: Automatic optimization
Elimination of maintenance costs
Reduced reliability
Guaranteed portability
questions.correctAnswer: Reduced reliability
questions.explanation: Poor readability and writability can make programs less reliable by forcing awkward approaches.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the lecture's cost criterion?
options: Consider only how much the compiler costs to buy
Consider only how many lines the program contains
Consider only the speed of compilation
Consider total costs including training, development, execution, reliability, and maintenance
questions.correctAnswer: Consider total costs including training, development, execution, reliability, and maintenance
questions.explanation: The cost criterion concerns the ultimate total cost throughout development and use.

questions.question: A language's official definition is complete and precise. Which property does this demonstrate?
options: Well-definedness
Generality
Aliasing
Expressivity
questions.correctAnswer: Well-definedness
questions.explanation: Well-definedness concerns completeness and precision of the official language definition.

questions.question: In the von Neumann architecture shown, where are program instructions and data stored?
options: In separate programming environments rather than memory
In memory, separate from the CPU
Only in input devices
Only in the control unit
questions.correctAnswer: In memory, separate from the CPU
questions.explanation: The lecture shows both instructions and data in memory, with transfers to and from the CPU.

questions.question: What limited resource causes the von Neumann bottleneck described in the lecture?
options: The number of source-code comments
The variety of predefined functions
The speed of the connection between memory and processor
The number of programming language keywords
questions.correctAnswer: The speed of the connection between memory and processor
questions.explanation: Instructions may execute faster than they can be supplied through the memory-processor connection.

questions.question: Which methodological shift does the lecture associate with the late 1960s?
options: The first adoption of JIT compilation for all software
The replacement of abstraction with machine-only coding
The start of object orientation through inheritance and polymorphism
Greater emphasis on people efficiency, readability, and structured programming
questions.correctAnswer: Greater emphasis on people efficiency, readability, and structured programming
questions.explanation: The late-1960s slide emphasizes people efficiency, improved control structures, and structured programming.

questions.question: Which pair consists of functional-language examples in the lecture?
options: Scheme and ML
C and JavaScript
Prolog and COBOL
JSTL and XSLT
questions.correctAnswer: Scheme and ML
questions.explanation: Scheme and ML appear in the functional category, where computation uses function application.

questions.question: Why are object-oriented languages included within the lecture's imperative category?
options: Every object-oriented language is a markup extension
They can still use variables, assignments, and iteration
Object orientation eliminates all mutable state
Inheritance requires pure interpretation
questions.correctAnswer: They can still use variables, assignments, and iteration
questions.explanation: The lecture's imperative category includes languages supporting object orientation as well as scripting and visual languages.

questions.question: C++ pointers illustrate a trade-off between which properties?
options: Readability and compiler speed
Generality and language standardization
Writability or flexibility and reliability
Portability and well-definedness
questions.correctAnswer: Writability or flexibility and reliability
questions.explanation: Pointers provide flexibility but can make reliable programming harder; this is the lecture's third trade-off.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the main compiler phases listed in the lecture?
options: Code generation, lexical analysis, loading, syntax analysis
Loading, macro expansion, execution, lexical analysis
Syntax analysis, execution, lexical analysis, interpretation
Lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, code generation
questions.correctAnswer: Lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, code generation
questions.explanation: The compilation slide lists these four phases in order, ending with machine-code generation.

questions.question: What is a load module, also called an executable image, in the lecture?
options: User code and system code together
Only the original source characters
Only a parse tree
Only a list of preprocessor macros
questions.correctAnswer: User code and system code together
questions.explanation: The lecture defines the executable image as the combined user and system code.

questions.question: Which statement best describes pure interpretation in the lecture's implementation model?
options: The source program is permanently replaced by an executable image
An interpreter executes the source program without first producing a separate compiled machine-code program
All source code must be compiled to native code before execution
Only a linker can execute the program
questions.correctAnswer: An interpreter executes the source program without first producing a separate compiled machine-code program
questions.explanation: The pure interpretation model passes source and input to an interpreter, without a separate compilation stage.

questions.question: Why did the lecture's early Java hybrid implementation support portability?
options: Java programs needed no run-time system
Every computer used the same operating system
Bytecode could run wherever a suitable JVM was available
Bytecode was identical to every CPU's native instruction set
questions.correctAnswer: Bytecode could run wherever a suitable JVM was available
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the JVM as a bytecode interpreter and run-time system supporting execution across machines.

questions.question: What is a programming environment?
options: A single rule for type checking
The final output of lexical analysis
A memory cell modeled by a variable
A collection of tools used in software development
questions.correctAnswer: A collection of tools used in software development
questions.explanation: Programming environments collect development tools; the lecture gives UNIX, Visual Studio .NET, and NetBeans examples.
